report: When the surgeon probed his temporal lobe, he heard his mother telling an aunt to come up that night. A probe at the next point gave the same conversation, and he said it was over the telephone. Another point gave her voice telling his brother that his coat was on backwards.

When her temporal lobe was probed, she heard a faint voice far away, then a name called three times. She said it was her husband’s name. Seven minutes later the same point was probed four more times and gave nothing.
Under the probe she heard many people shouting at her. When the point was probed again she said they were her mother and brothers, and she asked for it to stop.
When the surgeon probed his temporal lobe, he heard a man’s voice in a pool room telling him to get out. He later confirmed that this had happened.
A probe on the first temporal convolution made her hear someone speaking on the telephone.

Repeated probes at one point made her hear music that sounded as if it came from a radio. She could not name it but said it was familiar. She hummed it, and the operating-room nurse recognised the tune as “Rolling Along Together”. Probes at three points close by gave the same tune. The first point was on the upper, inner face of the first temporal convolution, on the cut surface against the insula.
Under the probe she heard singing, which she named as “White Christmas”, sung by a choir. When another point was probed she hummed a tune she knew and could not name.
When her temporal lobe was probed, she hummed a march, which was identified as the “War March of the Priests”. She said she had it on a record at home.
A probe made him hear a popular song from the radio, played by instruments. When the point was probed again he said the song had come back. His speech was in the right hemisphere.
A probe at one point made her hear singing, and at another a song that sounded familiar, as if on the radio. The legend of Fig. 9 lists four music points in this patient.
A probe 1 cm deep in the first temporal convolution made her hear a distant sound like singing, a group in the background, probably hymns.
When her temporal lobe was probed, she heard music in the background, like an orchestra or an organ.
When her temporal lobe was probed, she saw herself giving birth and felt she was living through it again.
A probe 3 cm deep made her see a dog chasing a cat in the driveway at home, which she had seen happen. Two minutes later a probe at the same point gave a forest fire she could not place.

Under the probe he saw robbers with guns coming at him, without sound. The report traces this to his comic books and calls it a fantasy. A probe at another point made him see his brother aiming an air rifle at him in the yard, and he felt scared.
When his temporal lobe was probed, he saw a man coming through a fence at a baseball game, which he said he had seen.
Probes at the back of her temporal lobe made her see a friend she had met on the street, then a machine she had seen before, then the nurses on her ward.
A probe brought footsteps and company, which he placed in a dance hall. Then came a scene at the seashore, with a woman talking to a child. His speech was in the right hemisphere.

When the surgeon probed her temporal lobe, she heard a mother calling her little boy, which seemed to have happened years before. She said it was somebody from the neighbourhood where she lived. A probe at another point gave voices along a river she knew, and she thought she saw the river. Another gave an office she knew, with desks, and a man leaning on one of them and calling to her.

One point gave different things when it was probed again and again: a piano playing a song he had once sung, then someone speaking, then “Oh Marie, Oh Marie”, the theme song of a radio programme, of which he sang the refrain.
Probes brought two scenes he knew, and then music from the stage show “Guys and Dolls”, with the feeling that he was there.
A probe on the upper surface of the first temporal convolution, just in front of Heschl’s gyrus, brought friends laughing, in South Africa. He named two cousins.
When her temporal lobe was probed, she heard her elder son speaking, with the noises of the neighbourhood behind him. Ten days later she said it had felt more real than a memory.
Under the probe she heard her mother shouting at her baby sister, and she saw them both. Another response was her parents talking and singing Christmas carols, and she saw them briefly.

Probes at several points gave what she called a flash-back. One reminded her of a football game, another of the time her mother went into hospital. A probe 3 cm deep, in the region of the amygdala, set her thinking about her dog.
A probe on the cut upper surface of the first temporal convolution, inside the fissure, gave him a dream. He said it was not like his usual attacks.
A probe on the lower face of the first temporal convolution gave her a very familiar memory.
When his temporal lobe was probed, he had a thought he had had before, like the start of one of his attacks.
A probe gave her terror for an instant, of the kind she had in her attacks. Probes at other points in the same patient gave singing.
Under the probe he felt very scared and said this feeling was his attack. Thirteen minutes later a probe at the same point made him say he was going to die.
While the probe made her hear voices shouting at her, she felt that something dreadful was about to happen.
